prompt:
You are a precise visual grounding annotator. Inspect the ONE supplied image of an actual textured 3D object. Locate only the physical regions described below. The image includes a coordinate grid with 0.1 increments. Read x horizontally from left to right and y vertically from top to bottom. Return coordinates normalized 0..1000 over this ENTIRE image, margins included. Do not use the textual role name as a location hint: inspect the pixels. First identify the material and visible boundary, then place a TIGHT box. For a grasp interval choose the described distinct material/segment only; never the entire shaft and never beyond its physical end. For a functional surface choose the actual narrow effect-producing surface described, not its supporting body. A body, a face and its outer edge are different regions. State what you actually see. For functional regions additionally mark origin on the supporting material and direction_tip ON the effect-producing surface. Both points must land on visible object pixels; the origin may be outside the functional region. Do not point into empty space to illustrate a direction. For an edge-on, hidden or ambiguous surface use visible=false with a concrete reason; do not invent coordinates to complete the answer. Return ONE JSON object with an objects map keyed by exactly the supplied IDs. Each entry: {"visible":true,"box_2d":[xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax],"confidence":0.9,"evidence":"specific visible boundary/material"}. Only functional regions add "origin":[x,y],"direction_tip":[x,y]. Invisible entries: {"visible":false,"confidence":0,"evidence":"why hidden"}. box_2d order: xmin_ymin_xmax_ymax. Points are always [x,y]. Before returning, visually check every coordinate against the grid and the object boundary. Do not claim visibility from an assumed shape. ROLES:
{"grip_lower_haft": {"role": "grasp_region", "description": "Leather-wrapped lower wooden shaft, clear of the blade"}, "grip_upper_haft": {"role": "grasp_region", "description": "Bare upper-middle wooden shaft, clear of the head and its sharp edge"}, "axe_head": {"role": "functional_region", "description": "Sharpened outward-facing cutting edge of the axe head", "direction_semantics": "From the body of the metal head outward toward its visible sharp curved blade edge, not toward the flat poll or down the handle."}}
